extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and researchers interested in Jorge Luis Borges and his literary techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts principles, themes and techniques from Borges's life and work that inform writing short stories and poetry in a Borges-influenced, experimental/philospohical mode. Useful for writers studying his methods (Ultraism, metafiction, motif use, formal experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultraism principles (poetic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction of lyric poetry to its primary element: the metaphor. Elimination of transitional phrases, links, and unnecessary adjectives. Abolition of ornamental devices, confessionalism, circumstantial detail, preaching, and contrived vagueness. Synthesis of two or more images into one, thereby expanding their suggestive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Borges's 1918/1921 Ultraism summary: Ultraist poems consist of a series of metaphors, each with its own suggestiveness and encapsulating an unprecedented vision of some fragment of life. The movement aims to transmute palpable reality into an inner/emotional reality; the procedure (briefly noting discoveries rather than expanding them) does not diminish emotional force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness / 'briefly noted' lyrical discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyric discovery should be briefly noted rather than magnified and developed; emotional force is preserved by concision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ultraism emphasizes short, concentrated images and metaphors rather than extended lyrical development. Apply concision to preserve intensity and suggestiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate unnecessary ornament and confessional detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Abolition of ornamental devices, confessionalism, circumstantial detail, preaching, and contrived vagueness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gratuitous decoration, overt confession, extraneous background detail, moralizing, or deliberate vagueness that does not serve the poem/story's suggestive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesize images for suggestive power
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesis of two or more images into one, thereby expanding their suggestive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine disparate images/metaphors into compact fused images to multiply meanings and resonance within a small space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use recurring philosophical and fantastic motifs
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ motifs such as dreams, labyrinths, chance, infinity, archives, mirrors, fictional writers, and mythology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These motifs function as organizing devices to explore metaphysical and epistemological problems; recurrent deployment builds thematic density across works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep authorial opinions separate from fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: "I don't allow these opinions to find their way into my writings... keep them in watertight compartments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow fiction and imaginative work to have autonomy from the author's political or overt personal opinions; avoid didactic intrusion unless intentionally foregrounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce an enigmatic, hermetic tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that are "inbent and hermetic, with the oblique terror of a game whose rules are unknown and its stakes everything."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate obliqueness, mystery, and a sense of unknown rules to create tension and interpretive depth; do not over-explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design branching / multi-reading structures (hypertext/maze)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structures comparable to a book-and-maze that "can be read in many ways" (e.g., The Garden of Forking Paths — arguably the invention of the hypertext novel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create narratives that permit multiple readings/paths — branching chronology, alternative outcomes, or layered texts — so the text functions like a maze or hypertext.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat fiction as philosophical/scientific thought-experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Write "reasoned fiction" that sometimes resembles theorems with fantastical hypotheses and distills ideas in formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame stories as conceptual experiments: set strict axioms or premises and explore their imaginative/logical consequences to illuminate abstract problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intertextual devices and fictional paratexts (forgery/false documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ fictional techniques such as fictional forgeries, pseudo-translations, invented citations and paratextual masquerades (e.g., passing invented texts off as translations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of fabricated documents, false authorities, and paratexts can create layers of narrative authority, irony, and metafictional play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write with multilingual/translation-aware diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose with multiple languages in mind; deliberate use of Latin (and other cross-language elements) can act as a bridge between languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words and register aware of how they will read and translate cross-linguistically; consider etymology and cognates to achieve layered meaning for international readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate scientific and mathematical metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use scientific/mathematical concepts metaphorically (e.g., The Library of Babel illustrating paradoxes of infinite sets; references to fractal geometry, combinatorics, or quantum ideas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ technical concepts as metaphors to make abstract philosophical or aesthetic points more concrete and to invite disciplinary cross-readings; use them metaphorically rather than as didactic exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the reader an active participant
rubrics_metrics.description: Create texts that "turn the reader into an active participant" by inviting interpretation, reconstruction, or choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ambiguity, structural gaps, or interactive/forging devices so readers must assemble meaning, infer rules, or choose narrative paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inferring autobiographical basis for fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution against inferring an autobiographically inspired basis for content or tone; books, philosophy and imagination are as much sources as lived experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume stories directly mirror the author's life; emphasize imaginative construction over biographical reading when creating and interpreting fiction.
